3c3c43fe7fcfdb46.text: ALARA principle ALARA “as low as reasonably achievable” is the guiding principle for the use of diagnostic ultrasound. Qualified ultrasound examiners, using good judgment and insight, determine the exposure that is as low as reasonably achievable. There are no sufficient rules to determine the correct response to every situation. Therefore, it is the responsibility of the ultrasound examiner to keep exposure low, bioeffects minimal, and images diagnostic. A thorough knowledge of the imaging modes, transducer capability, System setting, and scanning technique is necessary. The imaging mode determines the nature of the ultrasound beam. Transducer capability depends upon transducer frequency, penetration, resolution, and field of view. It is the scanning technique of the qualified ultrasound examiner along with patient variability that determine the setting content throughout the exam. There are variables that affect the way the ultrasound examiner implements the ALARA principle. These variables include body size, location of the bone relative to the focal point, ultrasound attenuation in the body, and ultrasound exposure time. Exposure time is an especially useful variable because it can be controlled by the ultrasound examiner. The ability to limit the exposure over time supports the ALARA principle.

067921cb8c9ccb84.text: Important Information — Please Read Before Use Applying ALARA The system imaging mode selected by the ultrasound examiner is determined by the information required. Understanding the nature of the imaging mode being used allows the trained ultrasound examiner to apply the ALARA principle. Prudent use of ultrasound implies that the patient exposure to ultrasound is limited to the lowest output for the shortest time necessary to achieve acceptable diagnostic results. The ultrasound examiner uses the system controls to adjust image quality and ultrasound output. Reference materials (1) Medical Ultrasound Safety, American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine, 2014 (2) Acoustic Output Labeling Standard for Diagnostic Ultrasound Equipment, American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine, 2008 (3) IEC 60601-2-37: 2007, IEC 60601-2-37: 2007+A 1: 2015 Medical electrical equipment – part 2 -37: Particular requirements for the basic safety and essential performance of ultrasonic medical diagnostic and monitoring equipment (4) IEC 62359: 2010+A 1: 2017 Ultrasonics – Field characterization – Test methods for the determination of thermal and mechanical indices related to medical diagnostic ultrasonic fields (5) Marketing Clearance of Diagnostic Ultrasound Systems and Transducers, FDA, 2023

799d03fcee4c1866.text: 3. 1 Precautions for installation and connection Chapter 3 Installation and Connection Prepare the Ultrasound Center and ancillary equipment according to the usage application as described in “System chart and Compatible Olympus Ultrasound Endoscopes and Probes” on page

583e5f342721843c.text: 687. Also, refer to the instruction manuals for the ancillary equipment, and install and connect the Ultrasound Center and the ancillary equipment according to the procedure described in this chapter.

38a328f3b9aa343a.text: 3. 1 Precautions for installation and connection Ch. 3

4741cd6d019ccedd.text: • Review this chapter thoroughly and prepare the ancillary equipment properly before use. If the equipment is not properly prepared before each use, it may not function properly, and also could lead to an electric shock, burn, or fire. Also, continued use of the equipment when it is malfunctioning could damage the patient's tissues and cause bleeding, inflammation, perforation, or other adverse effects.

6a6f11266c8554b3.text: • Use the Ultrasound Center under the conditions described in “Environment” on page 690 and “Specifications”. Use of the Ultrasound Center under other conditions could cause a malfunction in the Ultrasound Center, and could also lead to a breakdown and a safety hazard.

1ff50a4b1ef312a2.text: • Be sure to turn off the power of the Ultrasound Center and the compatible ancillary equipment before connecting the ancillary equipment. Connecting the Ultrasound Center while the power is on could lead to a malfunction or a breakdown of the Ultrasound Center or ancillary equipment.

d01f14f3cbe4d86d.text: • Connect all the required connection cables before turning on the power to the Ultrasound Center and ancillary equipment. Otherwise, this could lead to a malfunction or breakdown in the equipment.

c1e5c6b85e5f0729.text: • Do not connect with cables other than those described in this chapter. Connecting with other cables could cause the Ultrasound Center to malfunction and could also lead to a breakdown.

1aa05fbcdf96bb84.text: • All cables should be connected correctly and completely. If the connector is provided with a screw, tighten it securely. If the equipment is used without making the proper connections, this could lead to a malfunction or breakdown in the equipment.

f4abc52fb502c413.text: • When installing or moving the Ultrasound Center, hold the handles on both sides firmly for transporting. If the Ultrasound Center is dropped, there is a risk of damage to the equipment or injury to the user.

d0af75f027e8875c.text: • When using ancillary equipment other than medical electrical equipment, connect the power supply of the ancillary equipment to an isolation transformer before connecting to the Ultrasound Center.

bd9135f99c17b6a5.text: • The cables should not be sharply bent, pulled, twisted, or crushed. Otherwise, cable damage can result.

79d064213355b12c.text: • Never apply excessive force to connectors. This could damage the connectors.

edb65b26a3e3b13f.text: For easier cable connections, put a cable color seal on a cable so that the color of the seal and the color of the IN/OUT terminal name on the rear panel are the same.

07f749fb6fd7c170.text: This section shows the procedure for installing the Ultrasound Center and its ancillary equipment.

9da2c1f1aff032c6.text: • Video system center  Section 3.9 on page 54

fa30eab231afa5be.text: • Do not block the ventilation grills on the side panels and the rear panel of the Ultrasound Center. Doing so could cause the inside and outside of the Ultrasound Center to become hot due to lack of cooling, resulting in a breakdown of the Ultrasound Center, a fire, or burn. Also, continued use of the Ultrasound Center when it is malfunctioning and some of its functions are not working could damage the patient's tissues and cause bleeding, inflammation, perforation, or other adverse effects. Ch. 3

6ca474eb7c6e452f.text: • Do not install the Ultrasound Center in areas where it will be exposed to strong electromagnetic waves (near microwave therapy equipment, shortwave therapy equipment, MRI equipment, radio equipment, cell phones, etc. ). Doing so could lead to a breakdown of the Ultrasound Center. If the equipment malfunctions during a procedure due to electromagnetic interference, it could damage the patient's tissues and cause bleeding, inflammation, perforation, or other adverse effects.

f353771d99af3367.text: • Install the Ultrasound Center on a level and stable surface. Otherwise, there is a risk that the Ultrasound Center could slip or fall, injuring the patient or user, or damaging the equipment.

0856048699e3886e.text: • When using a trolley (cart) other than the mobile workstations listed in “System chart and Compatible Olympus Ultrasound Endoscopes and Probes” on page 687, make sure that it can fully support the weight of the equipment to be installed. Also, casters should be locked in place. Otherwise, there is a risk that the product could slip or fall, injuring the patient or user, or damaging the equipment.

62d604ede46d095f.text: • Do not place any objects on top of the Ultrasound Center. Breakdown or damage to this equipment due to deformation of the casing could result in an electric shock or burn.

65f653d2bdfdb3c6.text: • If dust has accumulated in the ventilation grills, use a vacuum cleaner or similar tool to suck up the dust. Use of the Ultrasound Center with dust clogging the ventilation grills could result in a breakdown of the equipment due to lack of cooling, electric shock, or fire.

b97290d278b1faca.text: • Move while keeping sufficient distance from the trolley (cart), especially from the front and left/right panels of the equipment, to avoid hitting people, ancillary equipment, walls, pillars, and doors. Otherwise, this could result in damage to the equipment or an injury. 38 EU-ME 3 INSTRUCTION MANUAL

b95e4403623d0f3a.text: 5. 1 Precautions for inspection Chapter 5 Inspection Inspect the Ultrasound Center and ancillary equipment before each case. For details on the inspection of the ancillary equipment, refer to their respective instruction manual.

c655f2c4c2c0ce1b.text: • Read Chapter 3, “Installation and Connection”, and Chapter 4, “Function Setup”, and properly prepare the equipment to be used. If the equipment is not properly prepared before each use, it may not function properly, and it could also lead to a fire, electrical shock, burn, or other accident. Also, continued use of the equipment when it is malfunctioning could damage the patient's tissues and cause bleeding, Ch. 5 inflammation, perforation, or other adverse effects.

e8fd837413db6b57.text: • Before using, inspect by following the instructions in this chapter. Also, for ancillary equipment used in combination with the Ultrasound Center, inspect by following the instructions in the equipment’s instruction manuals. If anything irregular is found, do not use the Ultrasound Center, and take corrective action by following the instructions in Chapter 11, “Troubleshooting”. If an irregularity is still observed, contact Olympus. If you continue to use the Ultrasound Center even though something feels irregular, it may not function properly, and it could also lead to an equipment breakdown, electrical shock, burn, or other accident. Also, if the equipment malfunctions during a procedure, it could damage the patient's tissues and cause bleeding, inflammation, perforation, or other adverse effects.

8fda3b875331a083.text: The inspection procedure is shown below.

8a377931db80c08b.text: Connect the ultrasound endoscope, probe driving unit, and ultrasound probe.

97488e2e8ee4f3f7.text: Check that the Ultrasound Center power is turned on.

5538db35ee6f9cf8.text: Check that the endoscopic image or ultrasound image is displayed on the monitor.

9319dc6e9efc6aa3.text: Check the information displayed on the monitor.

51886f79e0f90322.text: Check that the functions are working properly.

466c96c4728c9ab9.text: • Check the ultrasound image  Section 5.8 on page 179

3d5df090ca856538.text: • Check the release function  Section 5.9 on page 187

3b9eaed385aabd8d.text: Check that the video system center is operating.

f57f1027af42ada0.text: Turn off the Ultrasound Center. (if the Ultrasound Center will not be used immediately after inspection)

9c61c48741b0590c.text: 5. 3 Connection with the ultrasound endoscope/ultrasound cable or the probe driving unit Connect the ultrasound endoscope or ultrasound cable and the probe driving unit to the Ultrasound Center.

72390bfe35845266.text: WARNING When connecting the ultrasound endoscope, ultrasound cable, or probe driving unit, make sure that the power indicator or ACTIVE lamp on the Ultrasound Center is off. Connecting while the ACTIVE lamp is lit could lead to a breakdown of the equipment. Continued use of the equipment when it is malfunctioning and some of its functions are not working could damage the patient's tissues and cause bleeding, inflammation, perforation, or other adverse effects. Ch. 5

43c26bb8421e1367.text: • Do not connect any equipment other than the ultrasound endoscope, ultrasound cable, and probe driving unit that appear in “System chart and Compatible Olympus Ultrasound Endoscopes and Probes” on page

c988e0df7d187e98.text: 687. Otherwise, excessive ultrasound output could occur, which could damage the patient's tissues and cause bleeding, burns, or other adverse effects.

e57d4c5405c18efe.text: • Make sure that the socket and connector are completely dry before connecting. Connecting while they are wet could lead to a fire, electrical shock, or an equipment breakdown.

6c3ffdb9e2b3fc4d.text: • When connecting the ultrasound endoscope, ultrasound cable, or probe driving unit, hold down the Ultrasound Center so that it will not move. Applying an excessive load to the connectors or socket could result in an equipment malfunction, electrical shock, burns, or other adverse effects.

62fd9a8587be3ed0.text: • Connect by referring to the instruction manuals for the ultrasound endoscope, ultrasound cable, and probe driving unit.

bed9b7e6ecec1afd.text: • Mount the supplied socket cap to sockets that are not being used.

80fca86285d2ce1e.text: Connect the ultrasound endoscope or ultrasound cable to the Ultrasound Center.

e816b086fadc1bc4.text: • Depending on the ultrasound endoscope that is used, it may be connected directly to the Ultrasound Center or through an ultrasound cable. Refer to the instruction manual for the ultrasound endoscope that you are using.

96e63512cafb6c94.text: 6. 1 Precautions for operation Chapter 6 Operation This chapter describes the procedures for conducting exams using the Ultrasound Center. For details on the operation of individual functions not described in this chapter, refer to Chapter 7, “Functions”. This instruction manual does not cover matters related to clinical procedures using an endoscope. This chapter contains only safety precautions and basic operating instructions for operating the Ultrasound Center.

479f2ccad13cf60f.text: DANGER When using spray-type lubricants, anesthetics, alcohol, or other chemicals, use them at a distance from the Ultrasound Center to prevent the chemicals from getting on it. The chemicals could enter the Ultrasound Center through the ventilation grills and cause a fire or a breakdown of the Ultrasound Center. Ch. 6

741d7831fe4c313a.text: • Wear protective equipment such as goggles, face mask, waterproof protective clothing, and chemical-resistant, waterproof gloves with sufficient length. Otherwise, dangerous chemicals, patient blood, and other infectious materials could pose a health risk to the medical practitioner or operator.

e4b6a10e9cbfc7aa.text: • If you notice anything irregular about the Ultrasound Center, do not use it. If you continue to use the Ultrasound Center even though something feels irregular, it may not function properly, and it could also lead to an equipment breakdown, electrical shock, burn, or other accident. If the equipment malfunctions during a procedure, it could damage the patient's tissues and cause bleeding, inflammation, perforation, or other adverse effects.

783f9e3bb6ad9b72.text: • If you notice any irregularity during use, immediately stop using the Ultrasound Center, and take corrective action by following the procedure below. Continued use of the Ultrasound Center while it is operating irregularly could harm the health of the patient. If the ultrasound image or endoscopic image is not visible or remains as a still image, and you do not know how to recover it, turn the power off and then back on after about 10 seconds. If using together with ancillary equipment, turn them off and on again by following the instructions in their instruction manuals. If this does not resolve the irregularity, immediately stop use, and slowly pull out the ultrasound endoscope or endoscope from the patient by following the instructions in the instruction manual for the ultrasound endoscope or endoscope. If another irregularity is observed, immediately stop use, and slowly pull out the ultrasound endoscope or endoscope from the patient by following the instructions in the instruction manual for the ultrasound endoscope or endoscope. After pulling out the ultrasound endoscope or endoscope, take corrective action Ch. 6 by following the procedures in Chapter 11, “Troubleshooting”. If the Ultrasound Center is still not restored to a normal operating state, contact Olympus.

0a02ff097777217f.text: • Do not use the Ultrasound Center in areas where it will be exposed to strong electromagnetic waves (near microwave therapy equipment, shortwave therapy equipment, MRI equipment, radio equipment, cell phones, etc. ). Doing so could result in malfunctions, electromagnetic noise at a level that could affect observation and procedures on the monitor due to electromagnetic waves, and loss of ultrasound and endoscopic images. If imaging is lost during a procedure, it could result in damage to the patient's tissues and cause bleeding, inflammation, perforation, or other adverse effects.

34c1783059d46795.text: • When using a high-frequency cautery power supply together with the Ultrasound Center, use the high-frequency cautery power supply compatible with the ultrasound endoscope connected to the Ultrasound Center. For details, refer to the instruction manual of the ultrasound endoscope. Use of a high-frequency cauterization power supply unit, other than one from Olympus, could cause high-frequency noise at a level that could affect observation and procedures on the monitor, and loss of ultrasound and endoscopic images. If imaging is lost during a procedure, it could result in damage to the patient's tissues and cause bleeding, inflammation, perforation, or other adverse effects.

618288a6bffe8fda.text: • Before using a high-frequency cautery power supply, confirm that the high-frequency noise is at a level that will not affect observation or procedures. Using without confirming could damage the patient's tissues and cause bleeding, inflammation, perforation, or other adverse effects. 192 EU-ME 3 INSTRUCTION MANUAL

ca154d03603ecb26.text: • Do not place a humidifier near the Ultrasound Center. Doing so could cause condensation to form inside the Ultrasound Center, leading to a breakdown of the Ultrasound Center. Continued use of the Ultrasound Center when it is malfunctioning and some of its functions are not working could damage the patient's tissues and cause bleeding, inflammation, perforation, or other adverse effects.

2d7061333ffdb263.text: • Endoscopic operations and procedures should be performed while confirming with live ultrasound images or endoscopic images. 251932ad5321ecf6.text: 6. 10 Disconnecting ultrasound endoscope/ultrasound cable or probe driving unit

7fcf82411d90e906.text: WARNING Do not disconnect the ultrasound connector while the ACTIVE lamp is lit. c3a0f3aeb2d489ec.text: 7. 4 CHE mode This function uses the harmonic components from the ultrasound contrast agent for imaging.

0dd28a98e0890b69.text: • When handling the contrast agent, follow the instructions in the contrast agent's package insert and the instruction manual. Olympus will not assume liabilities for the risks inflicted on the patients resulting from misuse or inappropriate application of the contrast agent.

0cee481e0b9738f7.text: • Contact the pharmaceutical company to confirm side effects of the contrast agent on the patient.

e790a681f3eb8f32.text: • If any irregularity is detected on the examination subject during use of the contrast agent, immediately stop the diagnosis and take appropriate measures.

5e6342030e93b526.text: • There is a risk of production of cavitation due to the interaction between the acoustic pressure of ultrasound and the contrast agent, and this may injure the patent’s tissue or result in bleeding. To avoid this, always use the minimum required acoustic pressure for the examinations. The ultrasound output can be adjusted using the ACOUSTIC OUTPUT key on the keyboard.

d3a68dccbb744adc.text: • Do not use SWQ while using the contrast agent. If SWQ is required, confirm that Ch. 7 microbubbles have sufficiently disappeared first. There is a risk of production of cavitation due to the interaction between the acoustic pressure of ultrasound and the contrast agent, and this may injure the patent’s tissue or result in bleeding.

f2f677ca5bd4fee8.text: • Cardiac rhythm disturbances during exams using ultrasound contrast agents have been observed in the diagnostic range of Mechanical Index (MI) values. See the specific package insert for the contrast agent.

211631f555c9f451.text: • The CHE Software option (MAJ-2381) is required to use CHE mode.

72d961b11c17cb1a.text: • Refer to “Types of ultrasound probes and ultrasound endoscopes and their available functions” on page 18 for the ultrasound endoscopes that can use CHE mode. 322 EU-ME 3 INSTRUCTION MANUAL

d755e12be3cddc14.text: 8. 3 Volume calculation in Mechanical radial 3 D scanning mode This calculates volume on the 3 D image acquired in mechanical radial 3 D scanning mode.

618ae296cff6c37a.text: * Ultrasound probes for 3 D scanning are not available in combination with the Ultrasound Center in the US.

c5e2565d8e7f525d.text: NOTE The results of volume calculation are estimates. Do not use them for diagnosis. Since errors occur due to the insertion shape of the ultrasound probe for 3 D scanning and the pitch settings for helical scanning, results may differ from the actual volume. Volume calculation by designating regions on multiple planes This calculates volume by adding up the areas of multiple radial planes calculated in the linear view.

43ccec5d3d07dd0c.text: • Volume can be calculated for up to a maximum of two systems.

0f1a09e83ba4da62.text: • This cannot be calculated in oblique view. Calculate after switching to linear view.

d814968a1f20f55d.text: • Trace and edit measurement can be used during area calculation.

7362f51a41f95a11.text: • It is not possible to calculate by mixing trace and edit measurements when calculating area. 488 EU-ME 3 INSTRUCTION MANUAL

8f1ba2bb79de7398.text: • The sequence of volume calculation is as follows.

629b57fab0e8debf.text:  Trace the areas to calculate on multiple radial planes, or perform edit measurement, and then calculate the areas.

3e6055a2831e96e4.text:  Add up the products of the areas enclosed on the radial planes and the distances between the radial planes, and calculate the volume of the region.

04a74a5d748710d3.text: 385. 3 Display the radial plane to measure the area by adjusting the linear view as describe in “  Adjusting the linear view” on page 386.

dab0e8b59c4bbbb0.text: 8. 4 Measurement functions in PW mode Measurement of various values by tracing Pulsed Wave Doppler waveform This calculates average flow velocity and other values by tracing the Pulsed Wave Doppler waveform. Tracing methods include automatic tracing and sector tracing.

9fa99087ba446527.text: • Do not use values calculated by tracing for diagnosis. Since HR (Heart Rate) is estimated and used for measurement, the results may differ from actual values.

982145de1f6f2ccf.text: • Trace measurement performs various measurement operations after detecting the maximum flow velocity point in one heart beat of the Pulsed Wave Doppler waveform. The time required between the end of the operation and when the measurement value is displayed will vary depending on the load on the device. For this reason, the measurement result will be the measurement value from several heart beats before the displayed Pulsed Wave Doppler waveform.

c2e01747bdfa4630.text: • Automatic tracing cannot be used to measure the Pulsed Wave Doppler waveform of several heart beats and the Pulsed Wave Doppler waveform just after freeze. To measure using these waveforms, measure with sector tracing.

72fc25808e63d9e7.text: • Stabilize the Pulsed Wave Doppler waveform and use a suitable PW gain. If the ultrasound transducer or the PW cursor is moved with the Pulsed Wave Doppler waveform in a stabilized state, the Pulsed Wave Doppler waveform will be disturbed and measurement will not be possible. The measurement is also not displayed if the next peak cannot be detected. Ch. 8

6a5fcd46c3b0e1cc.text: • Automatic measurement of the PW trace works by detecting the maximum flow speed point and other factors from the Pulsed Wave Doppler waveform. For this reason, measurement results vary due to the PW gain and other factors.

65afc0b8905a41eb.text: • Freezing immediately after starting automatic tracing will make it impossible to play back cine review because no data will have been recorded that can be played back using cine review.

7e217de527eecf83.text: • The measurement results and the location of trace sector index on a Pulsed Wave Doppler waveform are displayed with the cine review function after freeze. They are acquired by operations after automatic tracing. For this reason, if they cannot be acquired with the automatic trace, then the measurement results and trace sector index cannot be displayed by the cine review function.

f889c08b1dc7989a.text: Sector trace This function allows for the manual setting of a measurement sector to measure while the Pulsed Wave Doppler waveform is frozen.

c1cd3c557f8e6d27.text: 9. 1 Summary of user settings The user settings function makes it possible to save parameter values regarding image quality and actions regarding trackpad operations for each user or observation goal. It is possible to register a new entry or edit, copy, or delete existing settings. The user settings saved for each ultrasound endoscope and ultrasound probe at the time of device delivery are referred to as standard settings. User settings newly created or edited and saved by the user are referred to as custom settings. Up to ten custom settings can be registered for each ultrasound endoscope and ultrasound probe, respectively. 7123748a18a1e235.text: • When patient debris enters a hole or gap of this instrument, contact Olympus without disinfecting it. If you try to disinfect by force, the disinfectant solution will get inside this instrument, causing fire and malfunction of this instrument.

d0b7af402b3473e9.text: • Do not apply spray-type medical agents directly to the Ultrasound Center. This can cause the chemicals to enter the interior of the Ultrasound Center through the ventilation holes, and may result in a fire or malfunctioning of the Ultrasound Center.

dd0eef0cad13adea.text: • When reprocessing the Ultrasound Center and/or keyboard, follow the policies at your national or local guidelines, and the chemical manufacturers' instructions, and always wear appropriate personal protection equipment. Failure to wear protective equipment may result in infection from materials adhering to the Ultrasound Center and/or the keyboard.

43db2b80a8483b84.text: • Using a disinfectant solution other than those specified in this instruction may result in insufficient disinfecting effect.

931c9b54747e95a6.text: • If patient debris directly or indirectly adhere to this instrument, disinfection has to be performed within 1 hour after the patient procedure. Patient debris will begin to dry and solidify, hindering effective removal and reprocessing efficacy.

71233ee45a1cde6c.text: • Insufficiently reprocessing for this instrument may pose an infection control risk to the patients and/or operators who touch it.

7d4e7814dc54ccaa.text: • Do not disinfect connectors or the power inlet. Disinfecting these parts can deform or corrode the contacts, resulting in contact failure that can cause malfunctioning of the Ultrasound Center and/or the keyboard, a fire, or electric shock.

487066230cca592b.text: • Do not soak the Ultrasound Center and/or the keyboard in water, or sterilize it with an autoclave or gas. This can cause malfunctioning of the Ultrasound Center and/or the keyboard, a fire, or electric shock.

fb7c4a5d4b0eab43.text: • Clean and vacuum dust from the ventilation grilles using a vacuum cleaner, when necessary. Otherwise, the Ultrasound Center may break down and get damaged from overheating.

39bcb75c6e144f04.text: • Wipe the Ultrasound Center and/or the keyboard using the lint-free cloth moistend with the detergent solution or the disinfectant solution, and then fully dry it off Ch. 10 before using it again. Using the Ultrasound Center and/or the keyboard while it is still wet can cause a fire or electric shock.

95d3e6cb1714e479.text: This chapter describes the workflow for reprocessing the Ultrasound Center and the keyboard.

Otherwise, be sure to follow the next step. 3 If disinfection is necessary according to national, local, or facility standards, refer to “  Disinfection”. Otherwise, refer to “  Cleaning”.

604edf7f7991acc2.text: Follow the usage (temperature, use life) and amount (concentration) provided by detergent solution manufacturers and disinfectant solution manufacturers. Failure to follow manufacturers’ instructions may result in insufficient cleaning and disinfection effect.

79d9b0abe173e7d9.text: Wipe remaining detergent solution and disinfectant solution according to instructions of detergent solution manufacturers or disinfectant solution manufacturers. Failure to do so may adversely affect the human body or this instrument.

cd25687a68abfb14.text: 1 Turn OFF the Ultrasound Center and disconnect the power cord(s) of the Ultrasound Center and/or the keyboard (MAJ-2380) from the healthcare facility grade wall mains outlet. 2 Prepare a lint-free cloth moistened with neutral detergent solution.

63169500faafeb5e.text: Figure 10.1 3 Wipe the Ultrasound Center and/or the keyboard using the lint-free cloth moistened with the detergent solution for the time specified by the detergent manufacturer, until there is no visible patient debris that remains on both the lint-free cloth and the Ultrasound Center and/or the keyboard. Replace the lint-free cloth as needed. 4 Moisten a lint-free cloth with utility water and wipe the Ultrasound Center and/or the keyboard to remove detergent residuals. 5 Wipe it with a dry clean lint-free cloth.

c20a39f0d6ac5290.text: 6 Prepare another lint-free cloth moistened with disinfectant solution (DEC-AHOL WFI [70% isopropyl alcohol] or Clorox Healthcare Bleach Germicidal Cleaner [0.65% sodium hypochlorite]).

815b5c919f4c68b9.text: Figure 10.2 7 Disinfect the surfaces, where patient debris adhere to previously (see Step 3), by wiping with the lint-free cloth moistened with the surface disinfectant solution. When using the DEC-AHOL WLI, wipe the surfaces for 15 minutes while keeping the surfaces completely wet. Change the cloth to a new cloth every 3 minutes. When using the Clorox Healthcare Bleach Germicidal Cleaner, wipe the surfaces for 2 minutes while keeping the surfaces completely wet. Change the cloth to a new cloth at 1 minute. 8 If any surface of the Ultrasound Center and/or the keyboard (MAJ-2380) remains wet, wipe it with a dry lint-free cloth and let it dry thoroughly.

e995f46d8094d95f.text: 11. 4 Returning the Ultrasound Center for repair Before returning the Ultrasound Center for repair, contact Olympus. Describe how the problem occurred and provide details. Malfunctions listed in the warranty are repaired without charge for the duration of the warranty period. Be sure to include the warranty form when sending the Ultrasound Center. If the warranty form is not attached, a fee will be charged for the repairs. Please note that even if the repairs are free of charge, the customer is still liable for the cost of shipping.

f3579e3353a0b327.text: • This instrument is to be repaired by Olympus technicians only. Olympus is not liable for any injury or damage which occurs as a result of repairs attempted by non-Olympus personnel.

fa41ed047d14f9c6.text: • Before sending the Ultrasound Center out for repairs, move the image data in internal memory to an external storage device. All image data will be cleared during the repair process. Ch. 11

TI Thermal Index (TI) is the ratio of attenuated output power at a specified point to the attenuated output power required to raise the temperature at that point in a specific tissue model by 1C. TIB Thermal index for applications such as foetal (second and third trimester), in which the ultrasound beam passes through soft tissue and a focal region is in the immediate vicinity of bone. c875d3aa9889738b.text: • It is the responsibility of the operator to understand the risk of the output of the Ultrasound Center, and to act appropriately in order to obtain the needed diagnostic information with the minimum risk to the patient. To be able to do so, we describe interpretation of the displayed ultrasonic exposure parameters, Thermal Index and Mechanical Index.

ac0f3a736b865b7d.text: • The relationship of various acoustic output parameters (for example, acoustic intensity, acoustic pressure, power, etc. ) to biological endpoints is not presently fully understood. Evidence to date has identified two fundamental mechanisms, thermal and mechanical, by which ultrasound may induce bioeffects in certain cases alteration or damage to tissue.

e98f697fae0ac868.text: • The temperature rise and the possibility of cavitation seem to depend on such factors as the total energy output, the mode, the shape of the ultrasound beam, the position of the focus, the center frequency, the shape of the waveform, the pulse repetition frequency, and the duty factor. The TI and MI are indices designed to give the user instant information about the potential for thermal or mechanical bioeffects. Because the MI and TI indices reflect instantaneous output conditions, they do not take into account the cumulative effects (especially heating) of the total examination time. It is relevant to indicate that shortening insonation times can give a large safety margin under some conditions (wide, scanning beams in soft tissue) but no significant margin under other conditions (narrow, non-scanning beams on bone)

03a09f18a949dc40.text: • The MI is intended to give a relative indication of the potential for mechanical bioeffects such as cavitation.

8b18b601393bafda.text: • The TI gives a relative indication of the potential for temperature increase at a specific point along the ultrasound beam. The reason for the term “relative” is that the assumed conditions for heating in tissue are so complex that any single index or model cannot be expected to give the actual increase in temperature for all possible conditions and tissue types. Thus, for a particular beamshape, a TI of 2 represents a higher temperature rise than a TI of 1, but does not necessarily represent a rise of 2C. The important point about the TI is that it is designed to make the operator aware of the possible temperature rise at a particular point in tissue.

edf04c2024997323.text: • What the indices do provide is an indication of the conditions that are more likely than others to produce thermal and/or mechanical effects.

97603874ecaaff4e.text: • The modeling for predicting TI assumes some cooling by blood perfusion. For applications where poorly perfused tissues are expected, the TI may underestimate the possible worst-case temperature rise, and again the TI should be maintained at a lower value. App. Conversely, when scanning organs known to be well perfused, such as hepatic, cardiac or vascular structures, the value of TI may overestimate the temperature rise.

c809fa138854c5f5.text: • In clinical application where the TIS has been selected to be shown on the screen, it may well be more appropriate to inform the operator to pay attention to the value of TIB. Examples are for breast scanning, when ribs may be exposed, and for vascular studies when vessels lie close to bone surfaces. 732 EU-ME 3 INSTRUCTION MANUAL

cb3d7545d3a350a0.text: • The assumption is made that the surface heating in soft tissue scanning mode is always larger than the worst-case bone heating at depth. This assumption may not be universally true, and for this reason TI values in both B-mode and Doppler imaging modes in second and third trimester scanning must be interpreted with caution.

14f682ab1f04f72c.text: • The TI values in scanning mode predict heating in tissue next to the transducer surface due only to the energy absorbed from the beam. No correction is made for the heating of the transducer itself. The same is true for transcranial transducers and smaller unscanned transducers where the heating is also predicted next to the transducer.

76fd47f99757d9b0.text: • The MI becomes important at a gas/soft tissue interface. Most critically is with the use of contrast materials when most attention should be made to limit MI.

f3df169e59d19f7f.text: Dual-screen display This function displays two ultrasound images of different modes side by side on the monitor. This is used in PW mode, FLOW mode, ELST, mode, and CHE mode. Stroke The movement range of helical scanning in the direction of the insertion axis. Pitch The movement interval of helical scanning in the direction of the insertion axis. Live Status where ultrasound transmission is performed and the ultrasound image is displayed in real time. Freeze Status where ultrasound transmission is stopped and the ultrasound image acquired just before is displayed. Release This function records the image displayed on the monitor as a still image on ancillary equipment (e. g. , color video printer). STC (Sensitivity Time Control) This function adjusts the brightness at each distance from the ultrasound transducer. Focal point This is the convergence point of the ultrasound waves to be transmitted. The resolution is better near the focal point. s-FOCUS This function reduces the change in resolution with distance from the ultrasound transducer surface (focus-dependent) by combining the received signals obtained from multiple transmissions (aperture synthesis processing).

b70a1c21314501bc.text: Image processing that suppresses low-level signals in the received signals for reducing noise. Weak signals from the tissue are also suppressed. c51fae322218a3e7.text: MI (Mechanical Index) An indicator of the ease with which ultrasound can cause mechanical effects on a patient. Follow the facility security policy (ies) for storage and management of this instrument. ALARA principle ALARA “as low as reasonably achievable” is the guiding principle for the use of diagnostic ultrasound. Qualified ultrasound examiners, using good judgment and insight, determine the exposure that is as low as reasonably achievable. There are no sufficient rules to determine the correct response to every situation. Therefore, it is the responsibility of the ultrasound examiner to keep exposure low, bioeffects minimal, and images diagnostic. A thorough knowledge of the imaging modes, transducer capability, System setting, and scanning technique is necessary. The imaging mode determines the nature of the ultrasound beam. Transducer capability depends upon transducer frequency, penetration, resolution, and field of view. It is the scanning technique of the qualified ultrasound examiner along with patient variability that determine the setting content throughout the exam. There are variables that affect the way the ultrasound examiner implements the ALARA principle. These variables include body size, location of the bone relative to the focal point, ultrasound attenuation in the body, and ultrasound exposure time. Exposure time is an especially useful variable because it can be controlled by the ultrasound examiner. The ability to limit the exposure over time supports the ALARA principle.

3530f3ea393d5d54.text: Applying ALARA The system imaging mode selected by the ultrasound examiner is determined by the information required. Understanding the nature of the imaging mode being used allows the trained ultrasound examiner to apply the ALARA principle. Prudent use of ultrasound implies that the patient exposure to ultrasound is limited to the lowest output for the shortest time necessary to achieve acceptable diagnostic results. The ultrasound examiner uses the system controls to adjust image quality and ultrasound output. Reference materials (1) Medical Ultrasound Safety, American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine, 2014 (2) Acoustic Output Labeling Standard for Diagnostic Ultrasound Equipment, American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine, 2008 (3) IEC 60601-2-37: 2007, IEC 60601-2-37: 2007+A 1: 2015 Medical electrical equipment – part 2 -37: Particular requirements for the basic safety and essential performance of ultrasonic medical diagnostic and monitoring equipment (4) IEC 62359: 2010+A 1: 2017 Ultrasonics – Field characterization – Test methods for the determination of thermal and mechanical indices related to medical diagnostic ultrasonic fields (5) Marketing Clearance of Diagnostic Ultrasound Systems and Transducers, FDA, 2023

Dual-screen display This function displays two ultrasound images of different modes side by side on the monitor. This is used in PW mode, FLOW mode, ELST, mode, and CHE mode. Stroke The movement range of helical scanning in the direction of the insertion axis. Pitch The movement interval of helical scanning in the direction of the insertion axis. Live Status where ultrasound transmission is performed and the ultrasound image is displayed in real time. Freeze Status where ultrasound transmission is stopped and the ultrasound image acquired just before is displayed. Release This function records the image displayed on the monitor as a still image on ancillary equipment (e. g. , color video printer). STC (Sensitivity Time Control) This function adjusts the brightness at each distance from the ultrasound transducer. Focal point This is the convergence point of the ultrasound waves to be transmitted. The resolution is better near the focal point. s-FOCUS This function reduces the change in resolution with distance from the ultrasound transducer surface (focus-dependent) by combining the received signals obtained from multiple transmissions (aperture synthesis processing).
E. reduction (Low Echo reduction)

Image processing that suppresses low-level signals in the received signals for reducing noise. Weak signals from the tissue are also suppressed. Structure enhance Image processing that reduces speckle noise while highlighting the boundaries of structures. Smoothing Image processing that spatially smooths ultrasound images.

MI (Mechanical Index) An indicator of the ease with which ultrasound can cause mechanical effects on a patient. The higher the MI, the more likely it is to cause mechanical stress/damage on the patient. PIP (Picture-in-Picture) This is one of the methods to display endoscopic and ultrasound images simultaneously on the monitor. It displays a small screen within the screen. POP (Picture-out-Picture) This is one of the methods to display endoscopic and ultrasound images simultaneously on the monitor. It displays two images side by side. Operation pointer This is a pointer that is displayed on the monitor and used to perform various operations. The operation pointer changes its shape so that it appears as an arrow pointer (white arrow mark) when used on the menu screen, as a measurement mark (“x” mark) when measuring, and as a cursor mark (blinking square mark) when entering comments. Pointer A green arrow mark that appears on the ultrasound image when the POINTER key is pressed. Administrator This is the administrator of the security functions of the Ultrasound Center. When you log into the Ultrasound Center as an administrator, you can register and edit general users, reset passwords, set protected functions, and perform other operations. General user This is a user who uses the Ultrasound Center other than the administrator. To use the protected functions, the user needs to enter the ID and password that were set by the administrator. Tap An action where you touch the trackpad with your fingertip as if tapping it. Swipe An action performed by stroking the trackpad with a single finger. Flick An action where you quickly slide your fingertip on the trackpad. Pinch in An action where you pinch two fingers together on the trackpad.

Pinch out An action where you spread two fingers apart on the trackpad. Click Pressing the SET key or tapping the trackpad selects the position indicated by the operation pointer on the screen. Follow the facility security policy (ies) for storage and management of this instrument. ALARA principle ALARA “as low as reasonably achievable” is the guiding principle for the use of diagnostic ultrasound. Qualified ultrasound examiners, using good judgment and insight, determine the exposure that is as low as reasonably achievable. There are no sufficient rules to determine the correct response to every situation. Therefore, it is the responsibility of the ultrasound examiner to keep exposure low, bioeffects minimal, and images diagnostic. A thorough knowledge of the imaging modes, transducer capability, System setting, and scanning technique is necessary. The imaging mode determines the nature of the ultrasound beam. Transducer capability depends upon transducer frequency, penetration, resolution, and field of view. It is the scanning technique of the qualified ultrasound examiner along with patient variability that determine the setting content throughout the exam. There are variables that affect the way the ultrasound examiner implements the ALARA principle. These variables include body size, location of the bone relative to the focal point, ultrasound attenuation in the body, and ultrasound exposure time. Exposure time is an especially useful variable because it can be controlled by the ultrasound examiner. The ability to limit the exposure over time supports the ALARA principle.

Applying ALARA The system imaging mode selected by the ultrasound examiner is determined by the information required. Understanding the nature of the imaging mode being used allows the trained ultrasound examiner to apply the ALARA principle. Prudent use of ultrasound implies that the patient exposure to ultrasound is limited to the lowest output for the shortest time necessary to achieve acceptable diagnostic results. Also, continued use of the equipment when it is malfunctioning could damage the patient's tissues and cause bleeding, Ch. 5 inflammation, perforation, or other adverse effects.

equipment used in combination with the Ultrasound Center, inspect by following the instructions in the equipment’s instruction manuals. ALARA principle ALARA “as low as reasonably achievable” is the guiding principle for the use of diagnostic ultrasound. Qualified ultrasound examiners, using good judgment and insight, determine the exposure that is as low as reasonably achievable. There are no sufficient rules to determine the correct response to every situation. Therefore, it is the responsibility of the ultrasound examiner to keep exposure low, bioeffects minimal, and images diagnostic. A thorough knowledge of the imaging modes, transducer capability, System setting, and scanning technique is necessary. The imaging mode determines the nature of the ultrasound beam. Transducer capability depends upon transducer frequency, penetration, resolution, and field of view. It is the scanning technique of the qualified ultrasound examiner along with patient variability that determine the setting content throughout the exam. There are variables that affect the way the ultrasound examiner implements the ALARA principle. These variables include body size, location of the bone relative to the focal point, ultrasound attenuation in the body, and ultrasound exposure time. Exposure time is an especially useful variable because it can be controlled by the ultrasound examiner. The ability to limit the exposure over time supports the ALARA principle.

3. 1 Precautions for installation and connection Ch. 3

• Review this chapter thoroughly and prepare the ancillary equipment properly before use. If the equipment is not properly prepared before each use, it may not function properly, and also could lead to an electric shock, burn, or fire. Also, continued use of the equipment when it is malfunctioning could damage the patient's tissues and cause bleeding, inflammation, perforation, or other adverse effects.

• Use the Ultrasound Center under the conditions described in “Environment” on page 690 and “Specifications”. Use of the Ultrasound Center under other conditions could cause a malfunction in the Ultrasound Center, and could also lead to a breakdown and a safety hazard.

• Be sure to turn off the power of the Ultrasound Center and the compatible ancillary equipment before connecting the ancillary equipment. Connecting the Ultrasound Center while the power is on could lead to a malfunction or a breakdown of the Ultrasound Center or ancillary equipment.

• Connect all the required connection cables before turning on the power to the Ultrasound Center and ancillary equipment. Otherwise, this could lead to a malfunction or breakdown in the equipment.

• Do not connect with cables other than those described in this chapter. Connecting with other cables could cause the Ultrasound Center to malfunction and could also lead to a breakdown.

• All cables should be connected correctly and completely. If the connector is provided with a screw, tighten it securely. If the equipment is used without making the proper connections, this could lead to a malfunction or breakdown in the equipment.

• When installing or moving the Ultrasound Center, hold the handles on both sides firmly for transporting. If the Ultrasound Center is dropped, there is a risk of damage to the equipment or injury to the user.

3. 3 Installation of the equipment

• Do not block the ventilation grills on the side panels and the rear panel of the Ultrasound Center. Doing so could cause the inside and outside of the Ultrasound Center to become hot due to lack of cooling, resulting in a breakdown of the Ultrasound Center, a fire, or burn. Also, continued use of the Ultrasound Center when it is malfunctioning and some of its functions are not working could damage the patient's tissues and cause bleeding, inflammation, perforation, or other adverse effects. Ch. 3

• Do not install the Ultrasound Center in areas where it will be exposed to strong electromagnetic waves (near microwave therapy equipment, shortwave therapy equipment, MRI equipment, radio equipment, cell phones, etc. ). Doing so could lead to a breakdown of the Ultrasound Center. If the equipment malfunctions during a procedure due to electromagnetic interference, it could damage the patient's tissues and cause bleeding, inflammation, perforation, or other adverse effects.

• Install the Ultrasound Center on a level and stable surface. Otherwise, there is a risk that the Ultrasound Center could slip or fall, injuring the patient or user, or damaging the equipment.

• When using a trolley (cart) other than the mobile workstations listed in “System chart and Compatible Olympus Ultrasound Endoscopes and Probes” on page 687, make sure that it can fully support the weight of the equipment to be installed. Also, casters should be locked in place. Otherwise, there is a risk that the product could slip or fall, injuring the patient or user, or damaging the equipment.

• Do not place any objects on top of the Ultrasound Center. Breakdown or damage to this equipment due to deformation of the casing could result in an electric shock or burn.

• If dust has accumulated in the ventilation grills, use a vacuum cleaner or similar tool to suck up the dust. Use of the Ultrasound Center with dust clogging the ventilation grills could result in a breakdown of the equipment due to lack of cooling, electric shock, or fire.

• Move while keeping sufficient distance from the trolley (cart), especially from the front and left/right panels of the equipment, to avoid hitting people, ancillary equipment, walls, pillars, and doors. Otherwise, this could result in damage to the equipment or an injury. 38 EU-ME 3 INSTRUCTION MANUAL

3. 5 Connection of the power supply

• Do not allow the power plug to get wet. Otherwise, there is a risk of electric shock.

• Do not apply any excessive bending, pulling, or twisting force to the power cord. This could cause the power plug to come off or the power cord to break, which could result in a fire or electric shock.

• The power plug of the power cord connected to the Ultrasound Center must be connected directly to a medical socket in a medical facility. If it is not connected directly to a medical socket, the power plug will not be grounded, which could result in an electric shock or fire.

• Do not connect to a 2-prong outlet. Doing so can prevent proper grounding and result in an electric shock.

• Do not connect the power supply using an extension cord. Doing so can prevent proper grounding and result in an electric shock.

• Confirm that the electrical capacity of the medical socket to which the Ultrasound Center is connected has adequate electrical capacity that is larger than the total power consumption of all connected equipment. If the electrical capacity of the medical socket is too low, it could result in a fire or trip the facility's circuit breakers, causing all devices connected to the same power source to lose power.

• When using the mobile workstation, confirm that the mobile workstation has an electrical capacity that is larger than the total power consumption of all equipment connected to the mobile workstation's power socket. If the electrical capacity is too low, it could result in a fire or equipment malfunction. Also, the protective device of the mobile workstation may be tripped, causing all equipment connected to the mobile workstation to lose power.

• Ancillary equipment other than medical equipment must be connected to the power supply via an isolation transformer. Otherwise, there is a risk of electric shock or fire.

5. 1 Precautions for inspection Chapter 5 Inspection Inspect the Ultrasound Center and ancillary equipment before each case. For details on the inspection of the ancillary equipment, refer to their respective instruction manual.

• Read Chapter 3, “Installation and Connection”, and Chapter 4, “Function Setup”, and properly prepare the equipment to be used. If the equipment is not properly prepared before each use, it may not function properly, and it could also lead to a fire, electrical shock, burn, or other accident. Also, continued use of the equipment when it is malfunctioning could damage the patient's tissues and cause bleeding, Ch. 5 inflammation, perforation, or other adverse effects.

• Before using, inspect by following the instructions in this chapter. Also, for ancillary equipment used in combination with the Ultrasound Center, inspect by following the instructions in the equipment’s instruction manuals. If anything irregular is found, do not use the Ultrasound Center, and take corrective action by following the instructions in Chapter 11, “Troubleshooting”. If an irregularity is still observed, contact Olympus. If you continue to use the Ultrasound Center even though something feels irregular, it may not function properly, and it could also lead to an equipment breakdown, electrical shock, burn, or other accident. Also, if the equipment malfunctions during a procedure, it could damage the patient's tissues and cause bleeding, inflammation, perforation, or other adverse effects.

6. 1 Precautions for operation Chapter 6 Operation This chapter describes the procedures for conducting exams using the Ultrasound Center. For details on the operation of individual functions not described in this chapter, refer to Chapter 7, “Functions”. This instruction manual does not cover matters related to clinical procedures using an endoscope. This chapter contains only safety precautions and basic operating instructions for operating the Ultrasound Center.

• Wear protective equipment such as goggles, face mask, waterproof protective clothing, and chemical-resistant, waterproof gloves with sufficient length. Otherwise, dangerous chemicals, patient blood, and other infectious materials could pose a health risk to the medical practitioner or operator.

• If you notice anything irregular about the Ultrasound Center, do not use it. If you continue to use the Ultrasound Center even though something feels irregular, it may not function properly, and it could also lead to an equipment breakdown, electrical shock, burn, or other accident. If the equipment malfunctions during a procedure, it could damage the patient's tissues and cause bleeding, inflammation, perforation, or other adverse effects.

6. 1 Precautions for operation

DANGER When using spray-type lubricants, anesthetics, alcohol, or other chemicals, use them at a distance from the Ultrasound Center to prevent the chemicals from getting on it. The chemicals could enter the Ultrasound Center through the ventilation grills and cause a fire or a breakdown of the Ultrasound Center. Ch. 6

WARNING

EU-ME 3 INSTRUCTION MANUAL 191

• If you notice any irregularity during use, immediately stop using the Ultrasound Center, and take corrective action by following the procedure below. Continued use of the Ultrasound Center while it is operating irregularly could harm the health of the patient. If the ultrasound image or endoscopic image is not visible or remains as a still image, and you do not know how to recover it, turn the power off and then back on after about 10 seconds. If using together with ancillary equipment, turn them off and on again by following the instructions in their instruction manuals. If this does not resolve the irregularity, immediately stop use, and slowly pull out the ultrasound endoscope or endoscope from the patient by following the instructions in the instruction manual for the ultrasound endoscope or endoscope. If another irregularity is observed, immediately stop use, and slowly pull out the ultrasound endoscope or endoscope from the patient by following the instructions in the instruction manual for the ultrasound endoscope or endoscope. After pulling out the ultrasound endoscope or endoscope, take corrective action Ch. 6 by following the procedures in Chapter 11, “Troubleshooting”. If the Ultrasound Center is still not restored to a normal operating state, contact Olympus.

• Do not use the Ultrasound Center in areas where it will be exposed to strong electromagnetic waves (near microwave therapy equipment, shortwave therapy equipment, MRI equipment, radio equipment, cell phones, etc. ). Doing so could result in malfunctions, electromagnetic noise at a level that could affect observation and procedures on the monitor due to electromagnetic waves, and loss of ultrasound and endoscopic images. If imaging is lost during a procedure, it could result in damage to the patient's tissues and cause bleeding, inflammation, perforation, or other adverse effects.

• When using a high-frequency cautery power supply together with the Ultrasound Center, use the high-frequency cautery power supply compatible with the ultrasound endoscope connected to the Ultrasound Center. For details, refer to the instruction manual of the ultrasound endoscope. Use of a high-frequency cauterization power supply unit, other than one from Olympus, could cause high-frequency noise at a level that could affect observation and procedures on the monitor, and loss of ultrasound and endoscopic images. If imaging is lost during a procedure, it could result in damage to the patient's tissues and cause bleeding, inflammation, perforation, or other adverse effects.

• Before using a high-frequency cautery power supply, confirm that the high-frequency noise is at a level that will not affect observation or procedures. Using without confirming could damage the patient's tissues and cause bleeding, inflammation, perforation, or other adverse effects. 192 EU-ME 3 INSTRUCTION MANUAL

• When handling the contrast agent, follow the instructions in the contrast agent's package insert and the instruction manual. Olympus will not assume liabilities for the risks inflicted on the patients resulting from misuse or inappropriate application of the contrast agent.

• Contact the pharmaceutical company to confirm side effects of the contrast agent on the patient.

• If any irregularity is detected on the examination subject during use of the contrast agent, immediately stop the diagnosis and take appropriate measures.

• There is a risk of production of cavitation due to the interaction between the acoustic pressure of ultrasound and the contrast agent, and this may injure the patent’s tissue or result in bleeding. To avoid this, always use the minimum required acoustic pressure for the examinations. The ultrasound output can be adjusted using the ACOUSTIC OUTPUT key on the keyboard.

• Do not use SWQ while using the contrast agent. If SWQ is required, confirm that Ch. 7 microbubbles have sufficiently disappeared first. There is a risk of production of cavitation due to the interaction between the acoustic pressure of ultrasound and the contrast agent, and this may injure the patent’s tissue or result in bleeding.

• Cardiac rhythm disturbances during exams using ultrasound contrast agents have been observed in the diagnostic range of Mechanical Index (MI) values. See the specific package insert for the contrast agent.

• The CHE Software option (MAJ-2381) is required to use CHE mode.

• Refer to “Types of ultrasound probes and ultrasound endoscopes and their available functions” on page 18 for the ultrasound endoscopes that can use CHE mode. 322 EU-ME 3 INSTRUCTION MANUAL

safety_blocks.text: Dual-screen display This function displays two ultrasound images of different modes side by side on the monitor. This is used in PW mode, FLOW mode, ELST, mode, and CHE mode. Stroke The movement range of helical scanning in the direction of the insertion axis. Pitch The movement interval of helical scanning in the direction of the insertion axis. Live Status where ultrasound transmission is performed and the ultrasound image is displayed in real time. Freeze Status where ultrasound transmission is stopped and the ultrasound image acquired just before is displayed. Release This function records the image displayed on the monitor as a still image on ancillary equipment (e. g. , color video printer). STC (Sensitivity Time Control) This function adjusts the brightness at each distance from the ultrasound transducer. Focal point This is the convergence point of the ultrasound waves to be transmitted. The resolution is better near the focal point. s-FOCUS This function reduces the change in resolution with distance from the ultrasound transducer surface (focus-dependent) by combining the received signals obtained from multiple transmissions (aperture synthesis processing).

safety_blocks.text: MI (Mechanical Index) An indicator of the ease with which ultrasound can cause mechanical effects on a patient. The higher the MI, the more likely it is to cause mechanical stress/damage on the patient. PIP (Picture-in-Picture) This is one of the methods to display endoscopic and ultrasound images simultaneously on the monitor. It displays a small screen within the screen. POP (Picture-out-Picture) This is one of the methods to display endoscopic and ultrasound images simultaneously on the monitor. It displays two images side by side. Operation pointer This is a pointer that is displayed on the monitor and used to perform various operations. The operation pointer changes its shape so that it appears as an arrow pointer (white arrow mark) when used on the menu screen, as a measurement mark (“x” mark) when measuring, and as a cursor mark (blinking square mark) when entering comments. Pointer A green arrow mark that appears on the ultrasound image when the POINTER key is pressed. Administrator This is the administrator of the security functions of the Ultrasound Center. When you log into the Ultrasound Center as an administrator, you can register and edit general users, reset passwords, set protected functions, and perform other operations. General user This is a user who uses the Ultrasound Center other than the administrator. To use the protected functions, the user needs to enter the ID and password that were set by the administrator. Tap An action where you touch the trackpad with your fingertip as if tapping it. Swipe An action performed by stroking the trackpad with a single finger. Flick An action where you quickly slide your fingertip on the trackpad. Pinch in An action where you pinch two fingers together on the trackpad.

Customer should use genuine devices as ancillary equipment for combination of this instrument, considering leakage of personal information and falsification of data by outsider. Follow the facility security policy (ies) for storage and management of this instrument. ALARA principle ALARA “as low as reasonably achievable” is the guiding principle for the use of diagnostic ultrasound. Qualified ultrasound examiners, using good judgment and insight, determine the exposure that is as low as reasonably achievable. There are no sufficient rules to determine the correct response to every situation. Therefore, it is the responsibility of the ultrasound examiner to keep exposure low, bioeffects minimal, and images diagnostic. A thorough knowledge of the imaging modes, transducer capability, System setting, and scanning technique is necessary. The imaging mode determines the nature of the ultrasound beam. Transducer capability depends upon transducer frequency, penetration, resolution, and field of view. It is the scanning technique of the qualified ultrasound examiner along with patient variability that determine the setting content throughout the exam. There are variables that affect the way the ultrasound examiner implements the ALARA principle. These variables include body size, location of the bone relative to the focal point, ultrasound attenuation in the body, and ultrasound exposure time. Exposure time is an especially useful variable because it can be controlled by the ultrasound examiner. The ability to limit the exposure over time supports the ALARA principle.

safety_blocks.text: Center, and take corrective action by following the procedure below. Continued use of the Ultrasound Center while it is operating irregularly could harm the health of the patient. If the ultrasound image or endoscopic image is not visible or remains as a still image, and you do not know how to recover it, turn the power off and then back on after about 10 seconds. If using together with ancillary equipment, turn them off and on again by following the instructions in their instruction manuals. If this does not resolve the irregularity, immediately stop use, and slowly pull out the ultrasound endoscope or endoscope from the patient by following the instructions in the instruction manual for the ultrasound endoscope or endoscope. If another irregularity is observed, immediately stop use, and slowly pull out the ultrasound endoscope or endoscope from the patient by following the instructions in the instruction manual for the ultrasound endoscope or endoscope. After pulling out the ultrasound endoscope or endoscope, take corrective action Ch. 6 by following the procedures in Chapter 11, “Troubleshooting”. If the Ultrasound Center is still not restored to a normal operating state, contact Olympus.

safety_blocks.text: The TI values in scanning mode predict heating in tissue next to the transducer surface due only to the energy absorbed from the beam. No correction is made for the heating of the transducer itself. The same is true for transcranial transducers and smaller unscanned transducers where the heating is also predicted next to the transducer.
safety_blocks.title: The assumption is made that the surface heating in soft tissue scanning mode is always larger than the worst-case bone heating at depth. This assumption may not be universally true, and for this reason TI values in both B-mode and Doppler imaging modes in second and third trimester scanning must be interpreted with caution
